bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/accounts.rs (account types, accounts, typed credentials, in-memory store, error cases), springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (generic secrets only), springboard/src/bare/account.rs (local OS account), springboard/src/shell/login.rs (sign-in), bifrost-cloud account API (separate repo)
summary: Apple's Accounts framework is deprecated (landing page: for new apps, use the service provider's SDK). BifrOSt now has a pure model of its object set in springboard/sdk/src/accounts.rs: account types with an access grant, accounts, OAuth 1 and OAuth 2 credentials with expiry and an encoded form for the keychain, an in-memory account store with the official save, lookup and remove semantics, and the error cases the model can produce. Still missing: a store shared across apps, the user's access prompt, credential renewal, and the cloud account.

features.apple: ACAccountStore: accounts, account(withIdentifier:), accounts(with:), saveAccount, removeAccount, requestAccessToAccounts
features.note: AccountStore has accounts(), account(identifier), accounts_with_type, save (assigns an identifier, updates by identifier), remove and set_access. It lives in memory for the app's process; no shared store across apps, no completion-based asynchronous API, and renewCredentials is not implemented.

features.apple: ACAccount: identifier, username, userFullName, accountDescription, accountType, credential
features.note: Account carries the same fields. The local OS account in bare/account.rs stays a separate OS-level object that no SDK API exposes.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/accounts.rs (Credential::oauth, Credential::oauth2, oauth_token, refresh_token, expiry_date, is_expired, encode, decode)
features.note: Typed OAuth 1 and OAuth 2 credentials with expiry checks and a byte encoding for keychain.rs. Sub-second expiry precision is lost in the encoding. Storage through the keychain is left to the app.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/accounts.rs (AccountType, AccountStore::account_type, set_access); springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (per-app manifest permission keychain)
features.note: Types are registered and granted through set_access. save is refused with PermissionDenied for an ungranted type. The user's access prompt is not built, so the grant is set by the caller.

features.bifrost: none (is_expired reports the expiry date only)
features.note: No token refresh path. Apps refresh tokens themselves through springboard/sdk/src/url.rs (URLSession) if needed. The refresh needs a network service, which is out of scope for a std-only model.

features.apple: Account sign-in sheets and the 'create account in app' flow of requestAccessToAccounts
features.bifrost: springboard/src/shell/login.rs (desktop sign-in: password field, authentication through privd, lockout)
features.note: Desktop login only. There is no sheet an app can present to add a third-party account.

features.feature: Secure secret storage used for credentials
features.apple: Keychain items as the backing store of account credentials (Accounts keeps them in its database)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (add, get, update, delete of opaque bytes), springboard/src/keychain.rs (per-app encrypted store), springboard/proto/src/lib.rs (KeychainOp)
features.note: Per-app, encrypted with a master key on the same disk. No access groups, so apps cannot share credentials, and no user-presence protection. An app can store an encoded Credential there.

features.apple: Not part of Accounts; Apple's equivalent is Apple Account sign-in
features.note: The cloud account lives on the server and is not exposed to apps through an SDK API in bifrost-os.

Seven of the official cases are modelled: MissingRequiredProperty, AccountTypeInvalid, PermissionDenied, UpdatingNonexistentAccount, NotFound (AccountNotFound), CredentialNotFound, FailedSerializingAccountInfo. The other official cases depend on the system store, the keychain or the network. No error domain or numeric raw values.

gaps: No store shared across apps: the AccountStore is in memory for one process. Persisting it through the keychain and sharing it is still open.
No user access prompt (requestAccessToAccounts): the grant is set by the caller through set_access.
No credential renewal (renewCredentials, ACAccountCredentialRenewResult); it needs a network service.
No SDK API for the local OS account (bare/account.rs) or for the BifrOSt cloud account.
The official ACErrorCode cases that depend on the system store, keychain or plugins are not modelled, and there is no error domain or numeric raw value.
The framework itself is deprecated by Apple; new apps should use the service provider's SDK, so parity here is low priority.
